findings.explanation: The SearchResultSerializer is being relocated from src/documents/views.py (where it inherited from PassUserMixin) to src/documents/serialisers.py (where it only inherits from DocumentSerializer). PassUserMixin is a critical mixin that passes the authenticated user and full_perms query parameter to the serializer via get_serializer(). The policy requires object-level permissions enforcement: documents have owner and set_permissions that control view/change access. Without PassUserMixin, the relocated SearchResultSerializer no longer receives the user context needed for permission checks. The to_representation() method directly fetches documents by ID without any user ownership verification: Document.objects.get(id=instance["id"]) at line 809 has no permission check. With PassUserMixin removed, this becomes an unprotected object retrieval that bypasses the authorization checks the parent DocumentSerializer (which extends OwnedObjectSerializer and SerializerWithPerms) normally enforces through the user parameter.

evidence.content: All objects (documents, tags, etc.) allow setting object-level permissions with optional `owner` and / or a `set_permissions` parameters... If these parameters are supplied the object's permissions will be overwritten, assuming the authenticated user has permission to do so (the user must be the object owner or a superuser).
